name: England
description: Defend the English lands from the Danes, the Norwegians and the French, fight for the Holy Land, win the Hundred Years' War and end the Wars of the Roses.

missions.name: Invasion of England by Norway and Denmark, 1013

events.text: Enemy reinforcements have landed at Hastings.

mission.history: Fog and war have always lain over these lands. Britons, Saxons and Danes have fought here for centuries. In 1013 Sweyn Forkbeard, king of Denmark, brought a great fleet to England, and his Danes and Norwegians now hold the south coast and the Severn.
mission.briefing: Break the Danish host before it reaches London.
mission.victory_text: The Danes are thrown back to their ships, and London stands.
mission.defeat_text: Sweyn's banners fly over London, and King Æthelred flees to Normandy.

events.text: Cnut's fleet brings fresh Danes up the rivers of East Anglia.

mission.history: King Æthelred is dead, and his son Edmund, called Ironside, has been chosen king in London. Cnut, Sweyn's son, holds the Danelaw and has laid siege to the city.
mission.briefing: Relieve London before it starves, and keep Winchester out of Danish hands.
mission.victory_text: London is free. Edmund and Cnut will share the kingdom, and England is not lost.
mission.defeat_text: Winchester falls, and Cnut is crowned king of all England.

events.text: Hardrada's men march up from the ships at Riccall.
Word comes from the south: Duke William's fleet waits for a fair wind.

mission.history: Harald Hardrada, king of Norway, has sailed up the Humber with the exiled Tostig, beaten the northern earls at Fulford and taken York.
mission.briefing: March north fast, retake York and destroy the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge.
mission.victory_text: Hardrada falls at Stamford Bridge, and of three hundred ships only twenty-four sail home.
mission.defeat_text: The Norwegians hold the north, and Harold's crown slips.

events.text: More Norman ships land at Pevensey.

mission.history: Three days after Stamford Bridge, Duke William of Normandy landed at Pevensey and built a fort at Hastings. King Harold has marched his weary army back south.
mission.briefing: Throw the Normans into the sea before William can march on London.
mission.victory_text: The Norman knights break on the shield wall, and William's claim dies with his army.
mission.defeat_text: William is crowned in Westminster on Christmas Day.

mission.history: King Stephen took the crown when Henry I died, but Henry's daughter, the Empress Matilda, has landed in England, and her half-brother Robert of Gloucester holds the west for her.
mission.briefing: Take Gloucester and Oxford, and end Matilda's war.
mission.victory_text: Matilda escapes over the snow from Oxford, and her cause is broken.
mission.defeat_text: Matilda's army holds London, and England is torn for another decade.

mission.history: Acre has fallen to the crusaders after two years of siege. King Richard now marches south along the coast towards Jaffa, the port of Jerusalem, with Saladin's horse archers harrying every step.
mission.briefing: Keep the column together, take Caesarea and Jaffa, and hold Acre behind you.
mission.victory_text: At Arsuf Richard's knights charge at last, and Saladin's army breaks. Jaffa is yours.
mission.defeat_text: Acre falls back to Saladin, and the crusade is over.

mission.history: King John is dead. The rebel barons have offered his crown to Prince Louis of France, who holds London and half the kingdom. The boy king Henry III was crowned at Gloucester, and the old knight William Marshal leads his army.
mission.briefing: Relieve the castle at Lincoln, then drive Louis out of London.
mission.victory_text: The French are routed in the streets of Lincoln, and Louis gives up his claim.
mission.defeat_text: Gloucester falls, and a French prince rules England.

mission.history: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, Prince of Wales, has risen against King Edward I, and Snowdonia has closed its passes behind him.
mission.briefing: Take Anglesey, the granary of Gwynedd, and end the Welsh principality.
mission.victory_text: Llywelyn falls at Orewin Bridge, and Edward's castles rise over Wales.
mission.defeat_text: Chester burns, and the Welsh hold the march.

mission.history: Edward III claims the French crown through his mother. He has landed in Normandy with an army of longbowmen and marches for the Somme, with King Philip VI's great host behind him.
mission.briefing: Beat the French knights at Crécy, then take Calais as a gate into France.
mission.victory_text: The French chivalry dies under the longbows at Crécy, and Calais is English for two hundred years.
mission.defeat_text: London falls, and Edward's claim with it.

mission.history: Henry V has taken Harfleur, but sickness has cut his army down. He marches for Calais, and the flower of French chivalry waits for him in the mud between two woods.
mission.briefing: Destroy the French knights and take Rouen, the heart of Normandy.
mission.victory_text: Agincourt is won. By the Treaty of Troyes Henry will be heir to the French crown.
mission.defeat_text: Calais falls, and the English are driven from France.

mission.history: Henry Tudor, last hope of the House of Lancaster, has landed at Milford Haven with French money and a few thousand men. The Welsh are rising for him, and King Richard gathers his army at Leicester.
mission.briefing: March through Wales, beat Richard near Leicester and take London.
mission.victory_text: Richard falls at Bosworth Field. Henry VII is crowned, and the Wars of the Roses are over.
mission.defeat_text: Henry is driven back into the sea, and York keeps the crown.
